routing.teacher_review: Use when diagnostic evidence conflicts materially with other valid evidence or the attempt cannot be interpreted fairly.

gateway.principle: A readiness diagnostic guides support; it does not label or punish a learner.

conditional_unit.title: Foundations & Readiness
conditional_unit.record_rule: Unit 0 updates Refresh and Readiness evidence only; it never erases or downgrades Course Mastery, Retention, or prior completion records.

units.title: Number Systems, Factors & Estimation
units.essential_question: Numbers can be classified, decomposed, compared, and estimated to support efficient reasoning.
objectives: Classify natural, whole, integer, rational, and irrational numbers
Use factors, multiples, primes, and divisibility
Apply greatest common factor and least common multiple

units.title: Integers & Absolute Value
units.essential_question: Signed numbers describe direction, change, position, gain, and loss.
objectives: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide integers

units.title: Fractions, Decimals & Rational Numbers
units.essential_question: Equivalent representations reveal relationships and make different calculations efficient.
objectives: Convert among fractions, decimals, and percentages

units.title: Ratios, Rates & Proportional Reasoning
units.essential_question: Proportional reasoning compares quantities and supports scale, prediction, and fair comparison.
objectives: Use tables, graphs, equations, and double number lines

units.title: Percent, Financial Mathematics & Change
units.essential_question: Percent expresses comparison per hundred and supports financial, scientific, and civic decisions.
objectives: Find a percent of a quantity
Solve discount, tax, tip, markup, and simple-interest problems
Interpret percentage points and relative change

units.title: Powers, Roots & Scientific Notation
units.essential_question: Exponential notation describes repeated multiplication and supports extremely large and small quantities.
objectives: Apply powers of ten in science and technology

units.title: Variables, Expressions & Algebraic Structure
units.essential_question: Algebra represents generalized relationships and preserves structure across many situations.
objectives: Identify terms, factors, coefficients, and constants
Translate words and contexts into expressions
Use properties to rewrite equivalent expressions
Combine like terms and interpret structure

units.title: Equations, Formulas & Inverse Operations
units.essential_question: An equation states that two expressions have equal value, and valid operations preserve that balance.

units.title: Inequalities & Constraints
units.essential_question: Inequalities describe ranges, limits, choices, and conditions rather than a single value.
objectives: Graph solution sets on number lines
Reverse the inequality when multiplying or dividing by a negative

units.title: Coordinates, Patterns, Functions & Linear Relationships
units.essential_question: Tables, graphs, equations, and words can represent the same relationship from different perspectives.
objectives: Plot and interpret points in four quadrants
Build tables and graphs from rules
Interpret slope as rate of change

units.title: Geometry, Measurement & Scale
units.essential_question: Measurement and geometric relationships support design, construction, navigation, and scientific modelling.
objectives: Solve perimeter, area, surface area, and volume problems

units.title: Statistics, Probability & Data Decisions
units.essential_question: Data analysis describes variation and supports evidence-aware decisions under uncertainty.
objectives: Calculate and interpret measures of center

units.title: Mathematical Modelling Capstone
units.essential_question: Mathematics becomes powerful when learners define a problem, make assumptions, analyze evidence, and communicate limitations.
objectives: Choose a personal, scientific, environmental, financial, or civic question
Reflect on readiness for Algebra I
standards: IB MYP: Applying mathematics in real-life contexts
